successCriteria.description: The `LeaveStatus` enum exposes exactly five members: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, each with a string value matching its key.
The `LeaveType` enum exposes exactly six members: ANNUAL ('annual'), SICK ('sick'), EMERGENCY ('emergency'), UNPAID ('unpaid'), MATERNITY ('maternity'), PATERNITY ('paternity').
The `LeaveAction` enum exposes exactly seven members: CREATE, SUBMIT, APPROVE, REJECT, CANCEL, UPDATE, DELETE.
The `NotificationType` enum exposes exactly five members: LEAVE_SUBMITTED, LEAVE_APPROVED, LEAVE_REJECTED, LEAVE_CANCELLED, BALANCE_UPDATED.
The `EmploymentStatus` enum exposes exactly three members: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED.
The `AuditAction` enum exposes exactly five members: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT.

The barrel export `src/shared/types/index.ts` re-exports all six enums so that a single `import { LeaveStatus, LeaveType, LeaveAction, NotificationType, EmploymentStatus, AuditAction } from 'shared/types'` resolves all of them.

`NotFoundError`, `ValidationError`, `ConflictError`, and `UnauthorizedError` each extend `Error`, expose a `statusCode` property (404, 400, 409, 401 respectively), and set `this.name` to the class name.

`IBaseRepository<T>` is a generic interface declaring `findById(id: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<T | null>`, `findAll(client?: PoolClient): Promise<T[]>`, `create(entity: Omit<T, 'id'>, client?: PoolClient): Promise<T>`, `update(id: string, entity: Partial<T>, client?: PoolClient): Promise<T | null>`, and `delete(id: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<boolean>`.

`BaseRepository<T>` is an abstract class implementing `IBaseRepository<T>` that accepts the pg `Pool` from `shared/db/connection` (with an optional `poolOverride`), requires subclasses to declare `tableName`, and provides working implementations of all five CRUD methods using parameterized SQL.
Jest unit tests in `tests/unit/shared/types/enums.test.ts` verify every enum value exists and each enum has the exact expected member count (5, 6, 7, 5, 3, 5 respectively).

constraints: All six enum files must use TypeScript `enum` declarations (not `const` objects, not union types), matching the existing pattern in the codebase.
